Meet Urban Sports Club
We are among the leading platforms for sports and wellness in Europe, dedicated to inspiring people to live active, healthy lives. With just one membership we offer access to thousands of fitness and wellness experiences across the continent.
But what truly sets us apart? We believe our people are at the heart of everything we do. If you're curious about how we work, what we value and how you might grow with us, explore our Culture Hub & Career Opportunities .
*Big news: Wellhub and Urban Sports Club unite!*
Urban Sports Club is now a proud part of Wellhub, creating a global wellbeing ecosystem. Together, we connect 39,000 corporate clients and 97,000 wellness partners across 18 countries, offering millions of people even more ways to stay active and take care of their health.
The opportunity
We are looking for a Senior Product Manager for our Growth Operations team to build and scale the marketing technology and automation layer powering Urban Sports Club's B2C growth.
This role sits at the intersection of CRM, marketing technology, and data activation, with a primary focus on enabling and scaling our CRM infrastructure while extending its impact across paid acquisition, product, and partnerships.
You will act as the system owner and enabler, ensuring our tools, automation, and data are fully leveraged to drive efficient, personalized, and scalable growth.

You own the CRM infrastructure, optimizing Braze for scalability, lifecycle automation, and personalization
You build and scale automated CRM and marketing workflows to improve efficiency and reduce manual effort
You activate customer data by partnering with Segment to enable real-time audiences and data-driven growth use cases
You extend CRM audiences across paid marketing channels to drive retargeting, suppression, and lookalike strategies
You manage and integrate the MarTech stack, establishing best practices, governance, and scalable processes
You drive AI adoption by implementing use cases that enhance CRM, content creation, workflows, and personalization
You collaborate with growth, product, and partnership teams to deliver impactful, cross-channel customer activation
What you will need to succeed
You have 4–7+ years of experience in MarTech, CRM Operations, or Marketing Operations
You have hands-on experience with Braze, Segment, or similar CRM and customer data platforms
You have a strong understanding of CRM systems, marketing automation, and lifecycle marketing
You have experience working with marketing data, audience segmentation, and customer activation
You have a solid technical foundation, including APIs, integrations, and data flows.
You bring a problem-solving mindset with a focus on scalability, efficiency, and process optimization
You are passionate about applying AI to improve marketing workflows, automation, and personalization
What's in it for you
Free Urban Sports Club L Pro Membership + Friends and Family Discount: Stay active with free membership, plus discounts for friends and family.
Flexible Work Model: Enjoy a hybrid work setup, balancing on-site and remote work options to fit your lifestyle.
Extended Remote Work Options: Work up to 120 days remotely within the EU, the UK, and Switzerland, including 30 days outside the EU. You'll also have the option to desk-swap at our other European offices.
WorkOUT Life Balance: Take advantage of 30 days of paid vacation annually, plus two additional days for volunteering, flexible working hours, and complimentary access to our mental health provider Open Up.
Personal Development: Receive an annual budget of €1,000 for professional growth, with regular internal training sessions and weekly German and English language classes.
Engaging Team Culture: Participate in regular team and company events along with wellness initiatives that help you stay productive, healthy, and engaged in a hybrid work environment.
Urban Sports Club is committed to providing a friendly, safe, and welcoming environment for everyone who applies for a position or already works with us, regardless of their sports preferences, gender, gender identity and expression, sexual orientation, disability, physical appearance, body size, race, age, or religion (or lack thereof).

The Sr Product Owner plays a critical role in ensuring that a product or feature is developed with a focus on delivering value to the customer and the business. They act as a voice for the customer and are responsible for making key product-related decisions throughout the development process, including identifying opportunities to incorporate emerging technologies, such as AI-enabled capabilities, where they can improve user experience, workflow efficiency, and business outcomes.

Product Vision & Stakeholder Alignment
Translation: Work with stakeholders to translate future vision and requirements into clearly broken-down epics and stories; ensure all team members understand and align with product goals, including consideration of emerging technologies where appropriate.
Stakeholder Communication: Act as the primary point of contact between the development team and stakeholders; communicate progress, changes, and updates regularly.
Team Enabler: Work with one or more Agile Development Teams and act as a central reference and information source, guiding system/product functionality decisions.
Entrepreneurial Spirit: Demonstrate a track record of delivering results in fast-moving, demanding environments.
Backlog Ownership & Prioritization
Prioritization: Create and maintain the product backlog; prioritize features, user stories, and tasks based on business value, customer needs, market trends, and strategic opportunities.
Backlog Management: Continuously groom and refine the backlog based on feedback, changing priorities, and new insights.
Feedback Integration: Gather and incorporate feedback from stakeholders and end-users into the backlog; adjust as necessary.

User Story Development: Break down high-level requirements into detailed, implementable user stories that meet strong Agile standards and support effective workflows, automation, and decision support where applicable.
Acceptance Criteria: Define clear acceptance criteria so the team understands what constitutes “done” for each feature.
UI/UX Alignment: Partner with UX to ensure backlog items have wireframes and UI designs ready for sprint planning; provide design feedback, participate in design sprints, and support user acceptance testing.
Planning, Delivery & Risk
Sprint Planning: Participate in sprint planning to select stories and tasks; ensure the team has a clear understanding of work scope.
Release Planning: Collaborate with the team and stakeholders to plan and prioritize releases aligned with market needs and business goals.
Quality Assurance: Ensure the product meets quality standards by accepting or rejecting work during sprint reviews.
Risk Management: Identify and mitigate delivery risks; partner with the release manager on timelines, tough conversations, mitigation strategies, and transparent escalation to leadership.
Business Outcomes & Data
Business Case Support: Assist in developing and presenting business cases for new features and initiatives; ensure alignment with strategic goals and stakeholder expectations.
Data-Driven: Define KPIs and measures for features and capabilities to track impact and inform decisions.

Bachelor’s Degree in relevant field
4-7 years of relevant work experience
Experience with Product and Development tools such as ADO, Jira or other similar tools.
Healthcare and technical expertise are highly preferred, including experience with data, API integrations, and interoperability standards such as HL7 and FHIR.
Strong analytical and quantitative skills, with the ability to use data and metrics to back up assumptions, evaluate outcomes, and assess opportunities related to emerging technologies, including AI-enabled capabilities, where applicable.
Leadership and decision-making skills
Excellent communication and presentation abilities
Understanding of the industry, market trends, and customer needs
Strong organizational and time management skills
Strong collaboration skills, with the ability to work effectively across Engineering, UI/UX, Product Management, leadership, and internal and external stakeholders.
Travel up to 30%

About Provation
Provation is a leading provider of healthcare software and SaaS solutions for clinical productivity, care coordination, quality reporting, and billing. Our purpose is to empower providers to deliver quality healthcare for all.

Provation’s comprehensive portfolio spans the entire patient encounter, from pre-procedure through post-procedure, with solutions for physician and nursing documentation (Provation® MD, Provation® Apex, MD-Reports, Provation® endoPRO®, and Provation® MultiCaregiver), anesthesia documentation (#1 Best in KLAS Provation® iPro), patient engagement, surgical care coordination, quality reporting, and billing capture (Provation® SurgicalValet™), order set and care plan management (Provation® Order Set Advisor™ and Provation® Care Plans), and EHR embedded clinical documentation (Provation® Clinic Note).

Provation has a loyal customer base, serving more than 5,000 hospitals, surgery centers, and medical offices, and 700 physician groups globally, including 19 of the top 20 U.S. hospitals.

In 2021, Provation was acquired by Fortive Corporation, a Fortune 1000 company that builds essential technology and accelerates transformation in high-impact fields like workplace safety, engineering, and healthcare. For more information about our solutions, visit provationmedical.com and follow us on Twitter, Facebook, and LinkedIn.

Our purpose at Provation is to empower providers to deliver quality healthcare for all. To deliver on this commitment, we’re guided by our core values – Provation has a culture of CARES:Community - We have a shared sense of improving healthcare, enriching the broader world we live in and serve.

Accountability - We own it and get it done with integrity. Respect - We build diverse teams that collaborate and communicate with positive intent and trust. Excellence - We welcome new ideas as we innovate quality solutions. Service - We are passionate about putting customers first.

The eRA Product Manager within Notre Dame Research serves as the strategic owner of the University’s electronic Research Administration (eRA) ecosystem. This position is responsible for the vision, roadmap, governance, and lifecycle management of the administrative systems that support the University’s research enterprise.

The eRA Product Manager partners closely with Notre Dame Research Administration and Compliance, Campus IT, and external software vendors to ensure research administration and compliance platforms align with institutional priorities, federal compliance requirements, and the evolving needs of faculty and research staff.

In this role, the eRA Product Manager acts as a high-level consultant to University leadership, translating strategic research objectives into scalable technology solutions that improve operational efficiency, data integrity, compliance readiness, and proposal competitiveness.

Most immediately, the successful candidate in collaboration with the Associate Vice President of Research and the Director of Research Effectiveness and Analytics will play a defining leadership role in steering the University through a major eRA implementation, shaping the future of Notre Dame’s research infrastructure from the ground up.

Key Responsibilities Define, manage, and execute the product roadmap for the University’s electronic Research Administration systems, prioritizing enhancements and feature releases that streamline workflows and reduce administrative burden.

Serve as the primary liaison between Notre Dame Research Administration and Compliance, Campus IT, and third-party software vendors to advocate for institutional needs and influence product development.

Lead system governance and integration strategy for research administration platforms, ensuring effective data exchange between eRA systems, HRIS, ERP, and other enterprise applications. Oversee research data governance practices to establish consistent standards, improve data quality, and support reliable institutional reporting and analytics.

Configure and maintain system validations and workflows to support evolving federal regulations and sponsor requirements, including NSF, NIH, USDA, and other compliance standards. Collaborate with leadership and stakeholders to identify opportunities for process improvement, automation, and enhanced reporting capabilities.

Develop and maintain system documentation, business processes, and training materials to support successful adoption of system enhancements and transitions. Lead “train-the-trainer” initiatives and support change management efforts across the research community.

Monitor system performance, user feedback, and emerging industry trends to inform continuous improvement efforts. Support reporting and data visualization activities to translate research administration data into actionable insights for leadership decision-making.

Support audit readiness activities by ensuring accurate system configurations, data integrity, and compliance documentation. Participate in vendor user groups, professional organizations, and research administration communities to stay informed on best practices and emerging technologies.

Bachelor’s degree in Business, Information Systems, Research Administration, or a related field. 7+ years of experience in research administration, enterprise systems management, or a related field. 3+ years of experience in a leadership, Product Owner, Product Manager, or similar strategic systems role.

Experience supporting enterprise-level software implementations, preferably within research administration, ERP, or higher education environments. Expert understanding of the research grant lifecycle, including pre-award, post-award, and compliance functions.

Strong understanding of enterprise systems architecture, integrations, and data governance principles. Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional initiatives and influence stakeholders without direct supervisory authority. Exceptional analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to interpret complex data and identify operational trends.

Strong communication skills with the ability to explain technical concepts to non-technical audiences, including faculty and senior leadership. Ability to balance strategic planning with operational execution in a dynamic environment. Strong organizational and project management skills with attention to detail and compliance requirements.

Preferred qualifications Experience working within higher education research administration environments. Familiarity with eRA systems, ERP platforms, and SaaS-to-on-premises data integrations. Experience with reporting and visualization tools such as Tableau or Power BI.

Knowledge of federal research compliance regulations and sponsored program administration. Please include a cover letter and resume to be considered for this role. Salary up to $113,500, commensurate with experience. Applications due by July 27 2026.

About the role Automated video editing is an emerging category, and we're positioned to define it. Media companies want to turn thousands of podcast episodes into social clips. Marketing teams want to automatically create product demos for every release. Agencies want to process client content in bulk with consistent branding.

And they want to do all of that at scale. As the Product Manager for this 0 to 1 area, you'll build and own the platform that makes this all possible. You'll create APIs that let developers programmatically import media, run AI-powered edits, and export content.

In essence, turning Descript 's already powerful editing capabilities into infrastructure that media businesses can depend on.

What you’ll do Own the API and developer experience that lets teams create content workflows at scale Launch integrations that unlock new use cases: MCP wrappers, no-code workflow platforms, and strategic partner integrations Work closely with our Agentic AI team to influence what editing capabilities we build and how they're exposed through the API Define and grow this business line by shaping positioning, pricing, and go-to-market strategy with Sales and Marketing teams Who you are You’ve shipped technical products before: You have 5 or more years of product management experience shipping internal APIs, developer platforms, and foundational systems that enable other teams You build things from scratch: Building a brand new product means venturing into the unknown, and you find that energizing rather than scary.

You've taken products from 0 to 1, figured out ambiguous problem spaces, and created the playbook to make it successful. You start with the customer : Plenty of “AI products” start with the technology and they all suck.

You care deeply about understanding customers, and have experience in doing customer discovery and defining features that solve real problems. You are funny, creative, maybe kind of weird : Ok, this isn’t a hard requirement but Descript is kind of a quirky place and the people who love it tend to like that about working here.

So, just want to drop a hint early on. Also, the sense of humor is important because even though we take our work seriously it’s still just, like, video creation and editing. We aren’t flying rockets into space so let’s all have a good time. The base salary range for this role is $171,000 - $235,000/year.

This role

Liberis is in the middle of a meaningful shift. We started as a single-product business and are quickly becoming a truly multi-product embedded finance company, with different funding structures, revenue models and customer relationships sitting alongside each other in the same portfolio. That complexity creates real demand for better data, better insight and clearer thinking about how all of it fits together - with this role sitting at the centre of that challange!

As our Senior Data Product Manager, you’ll sit right at the intersection of product, analytics, engineering and senior leadership, helping define the data products that power smarter decisions across Liberis.

You’ll have real ownership over roadmap, prioritisation and ways of working, and your work will directly influence how teams access, understand and use data day to day. This role is a high-impact opportunity for someone who wants to shape how a business uses data at scale!

You’ll be joining a team with a broad remit and a genuine mandate to improve the data experience across the company, so there’s a lot of scope to make the role your own and shape the future of the domain.

You will own the data and insights product for Liberis, building the foundations that let our commercial, credit and operations teams actually understand the business they're running.

That means, thinking carefully about the entities in our data model, how products and customers relate to each other, how those relationships surface in reporting and analysis - and how it eventually all comes out in great dashboards, tools and self-serve capabilities.

This is about shipping products which are genuinely useful, not just technically correct.

Our Engineering Team is going through an AI-first transformation, rethinking how teams are structured and how they ship. Data, insights and analytics are a crucial part of that journey and you will be a key player in leading, innovating and rapidly improving our posture and capabilities at the intersection of data and AI.

If you like solving genuinely hard problems, bringing clarity to complex environments and building products that have visible business impact - this is the role for you!

Your primary job is to help Liberis's commercial decision makers understand the small businesses we serve and how they consider, use and perform across our product range. Doing this well requires a clear conceptual model of the business and a willingness to engage with stakeholders across the business, as well as taste and customer empathy in developing a great insights product including dashboards, insight tools and self-serve capabilities.

You will own the roadmap for our internal data & insight products. Working with stakeholders across commercial, credit, finance and operations, you will define what good looks like and then work with your team to build it. You will run prioritisation, manage the backlog and make decisions about where effort goes.

You will also spend a meaningful amount of time in the detail, reviewing data models and dashboards, asking hard questions about definitions, and making sure what we ship is accurate and trusted.

You will partner closely with the engineering side of your team on how data is modelled and structured in BigQuery and DBT, and with analysts on how it gets presented in Looker. You don't need to write production code, but you need enough technical understanding to be a genuine partner in those conversations. You will also be responsible for continuing to expand our partner-facing reporting, whereby partners gain visibility into their portfolio.

This role requires someone who can think clearly about complex data structures and translate that thinking into products that non-technical people actually find useful. The ideal person has strong conceptual thinking skills, great product instincts and enough technical depth to earn the trust of the engineers and analysts they work with.

· Proven experience in a senior data product or analytics product role in a business with real complexity

· A track record of helping commercial teams make better decisions through better data, not just shipping dashboards

· Strong ability to think about entities, taxonomies and relationships in data

· Hands-on experience with Looker and LookML and familiarity with best practices and scalable approaches to these systems

· Working knowledge of SQL, DBT and BigQuery, enough to engage seriously with how data is modelled and what's feasible, and to express your thinking in code-speak where needed

· Experience working with a multi skilled team of analysts and data engineers

· Clear, confident communication with senior commercial stakeholders

Support engineering teams in identifying and resolving complex technical issues.
Maintain sufficient technical depth to participate in design reviews, architecture discussions, and production support activities.

On-time delivery of roadmap commitments.
Platform stability, reliability, and performance improvements.

Reduction in production incidents and operational risks.

Homebound is on a mission to make it possible for anyone, anywhere, to build a home using technology. Created by an experienced team of construction, real estate, design, and technology experts, Homebound is transforming the residential construction industry by improving the costly and inefficient process of building a home.
We’ve created an entirely new way to build homes with technology powering every stage from start to finish to provide a seamless experience for our customers. Homeowners across the country can choose where they want to live, select a home plan that’s perfect for them, then personalize and buy it, all online.

Homebound has raised $150M in capital from leading venture capitalists like Google, Khosla, Thrive Ventures, and we’re scaling quickly in places like Texas, Colorado and Florida. Come build your future with us.

As Senior Product Manager - Field AI, you will own the forward-looking technology that brings AI to the teams building our homes. This is where the physical and digital worlds meet: your users are the Superintendents and Direct Construction Operators (DCOs) on the jobsite, and your product surface spans our mobile application, advanced onsite AI tools, automated data capture, and probabilistic construction schedules with insight analysis.
This is a role for a thought leader in applied AI. We are looking for someone with a strong point of view on how emerging technologies - computer vision, agents, LLMs, and multimodal models - can be applied in a physical, unstructured environment to make our field teams faster, more accurate, and more effective.

You don't need a construction background (though genuine curiosity about the built world is a plus), but you do need real experience translating frontier AI into products that work in the real world, outside the browser.
You'll own the roadmap, execution, and success metrics for the field AI portfolio, and you'll operate as an independent, cross-functional force connecting Construction Operations, Field Operations, and Engineering.

Own the field AI strategy and roadmap: Set the vision and execute end-to-end across the entirety of our field portfolio - from concept to rollout.
Bring AI into the physical environment: Translate the capabilities of computer vision, multimodal models, and agents into products that operate reliably on an active jobsite, where inputs are messy and conditions change daily.
Lead as a thought partner: Bring a strong, well-formed perspective on where field technology is going, and use it to shape how Homebound applies new technologies to the teams building our homes.
Embed with the field: Travel to Texas monthly to work directly with Superintendents and DCOs, run trainings, drive rollouts, and build the tight feedback loops that make field products actually stick.
Drive progress across teams: Operate independently and move initiatives forward across Construction Operations, Operations, and Engineering without waiting for a playbook.
Define product with rigor: Write clear, actionable requirements, establish evaluation and quality frameworks for AI features, and prioritize based on impact, effort, and long-term value.
Measure what matters: Define success metrics and run experiments to systematically improve accuracy, adoption, and field efficiency.

5+ years of product management experience, including ownership of a complex, technical product.
A track record of shipping applied AI products - computer vision, multimodal, LLM/agent-based, or ML systems - that took meaningful action or made decisions in production, not just chat wrappers or lightweight integrations.
Demonstrated experience applying technology in the physical world or in traditionally non-tech, unstructured environments (a strong plus).
Strong technical fluency - comfortable operating alongside engineers and ML teams as peers, reasoning through system tradeoffs, reading evaluations, and diving into the data to answer your own questions.
A self-starter and independent operator who thrives in ambiguity, moves quickly, and drives outcomes cross-functionally without heavy process.
A genuine thought leader in emerging AI - you follow the frontier closely and have a point of view on how to apply it.
0→1 product building: hands-on experience taking a product from concept through launch to real-world adoption.
Exceptional communication skills and the ability to translate seamlessly between field needs, technical teams, and executive leadership.
Willingness to travel to Texas monthly to work shoulder-to-shoulder with our field teams.
Interest in construction and the built environment is a plus; no prior industry experience required, but an expectation to learn the domain rapidly.

About Allica Bank
Allica is the UK’s fastest growing company - and the fastest-growing financial technology (Fintech) firm ever. Our purpose is to help established SMEs, one of the last major underserved opportunities in Fintech.
Established SMEs are the backbone of local communities - representing over a third of our economy - yet have been largely neglected both by traditional high street banks and modern fintech providers.
Department Description
Allica Bank aims to provide Expert Banking for Business Britain by providing excellent customer experience and pioneering technology solutions to facilitate this.
The Autonomous Lending tribe runs across multiple business lines including Credit Operations and Underwriting, with a mission to build AI-first lending origination journeys, automating origination capabilities, data flows, and underwriting and operational workflow management.
The tribe is a critical driver for Allica to continue to realise its vision of providing a market leading relationship-based banking experience, at a speed and cost to serve the rest of the market cannot match.
Role Description
The Product Owner will lead the work to define, deliver and manage AI-enabled products across our lending journeys, bringing together product design and thinking with a strong working knowledge of what today’s AI can and cannot do.
You will be accountable for the roadmap of your team and for the full product lifecycle: discovery and design, day-to-day delivery, launch and adoption by colleagues and customers, and how risks are addressed once a product is live. You will aim to build robust, automated and well-governed systems and processes that enable us to move quickly and innovate our lending and financing products in the SME banking market.
Whilst a lot of the market aims to avoid the complex nature of SME businesses, we are going for it head on, designing simple and efficient solutions to the most complex problems in the market to provide excellent and efficient customer experience. We aim for our external view of the lending product, as well as our internal systems to be the best in market which will allow us to scale quickly to serve more UK SMEs, while doing so in a cost-effective manner.
Principal Accountabilities
Responsible for innovation and building end-to-end solutions for AI-enabled lending product, origination, underwriting and operational flows
Lead a small cross-functional team (e.g. a full stack engineer and AI specialist) to deliver your roadmap
Continuously review business needs, refine priorities and iterate towards measurable outcomes – judged on fewer requests for further information, more applications decided with AI, less colleague time per application across underwriting and credit operations, and risk outcomes no worse than the equivalent manual journey
Prototype and experiment quickly – vibe-code working prototypes yourself, close enough to the real thing that an engineer can harden it into production code
Determine the accuracy of AI solutions by analysing the data yourself and building the verified “ground truth” datasets that results are tested against, working with underwriters and credit operations colleagues to agree what a correct answer looks like
Take responsibility for launch and adoption – briefing stakeholders, training the teams who will use the product, and closing the loop on the feedback they give back
Produce the written work that keeps delivery moving and safe – clear descriptions of what we are building and why, a record of the important design decisions and trade-offs made, and the assessments needed to get a product approved and live, covering risk, security, cost, data and legal considerations, and taking the change through the bank’s governance and approval process
Line manage, coach and develop your team, setting a high bar for delivery and for the responsible use of AI
Personal Attributes & Experience
Knowledge of commercial lending origination and underwriting processes, principles and systems
Experience in a fast-moving or high-growth business
Proven track record of delivering agentic and data-driven products into live use
Strong process design, implementation and automation skills
Hands-on familiarity with Python, SQL and data analytics tools, alongside LLM tooling, prompt engineering and AI orchestration – you do not need to be an engineer or an analyst, but you should be able to build something that works, query the data yourself, and understand and sense-check what AI is producing
Understanding of privacy and safety considerations when applying LLMs in production, and of how to prove and monitor accuracy once a solution is live – ideally in a regulated environment
Strong analytical skills and business acumen, comfortable digging into data yourself to size a problem, measure performance and assemble the reference datasets accuracy is judged against
Metric and outcome driven approach – setting the measures up front, tracking them once a product is live, and stopping work that is not moving them
Experience working with or leading product and engineering teams, and comfortable in ambiguous, fast-moving environments where the problem is as novel as the solution

We are expanding our Product team, and this role owns a slice of the internal product ecosystem our teams run the business on.
Your starting focus is the Media Buyer Automation Platform — the rules engine, pacing logic, spend controls, alerting, and workflow tooling that let a small team of buyers manage budgets that would otherwise require significantly more headcount.

From there, your scope extends across the internal tools that support the wider acquisition engine: marketing automation, reporting and analytics workflows, creative operations, and the new tooling we build as the business shifts.

We expect the exact portfolio to evolve, and we are hiring someone who wants that rather than someone looking for a single fixed product.
This is a hands-on builder role rather than a coordination role. Your users are colleagues, the feedback loop is short, and your work shows up in CPA, ROAS, wasted spend, and hours returned to the team. You will report to the Head of Product and work daily with Engineering, Data, Media Buying, Creative, and Operations.

1. Product Strategy & Roadmap
Own the end-to-end roadmap for the Media Buyer Automation Platform, including discovery, prioritization, specifications, delivery, adoption, and iteration.
Take on additional internal products as the portfolio grows, sequencing work across marketing automation, reporting and analytics, creative operations, cross-platform account management, and data reconciliation while maintaining focus on the core platform.
2. User Needs & Automation
Work closely with media buyers to understand their workflows and translate their operational needs into reliable automation for budget pacing, anomaly alerts, spend guardrails, bulk actions, and approval flows.
Identify manual processes that are consuming capacity across the business and evaluate whether they should be automated through internal development, external solutions, or left unchanged.
3. Product Development & Delivery
Write clear product specifications that engineers can build from, including edge cases, failure modes, rollback behavior, and a defined bar for completion.
Prototype ideas and build lightweight automations where this can accelerate alignment or address smaller workflow needs without relying on the engineering roadmap.
4. Adoption, Measurement & Collaboration
Drive product adoption through onboarding, enablement, documentation, and continuous feedback loops that ensure tools remain actively used and valuable.
Define and track meaningful product metrics, ensuring they are properly instrumented and visible, while partnering with Data on event taxonomy, attribution challenges, and measurement trade-offs.

Run experiments and staged rollouts to validate changes, particularly for functionality that affects advertising spend, before deploying them across full budgets.
Continuously evaluate and iterate on products based on performance data, user feedback, and evolving business needs.

We are looking for Product Managers with varying levels of experience to join SeatGeek’s R&D team. This role will own SeatGeek's Catalog — the foundational data layer that defines what exists on our platform.

Every event a fan can shop, every seat they can buy, every venue map they navigate, and every attribute that makes a ticket more than a dot on a map starts here. Catalog is the ground truth that everything else — shopping, fulfillment, and eventually attending the event — is built on top of.
This is a high-leverage, deeply cross-functional role. When the catalog is accurate, complete, and fresh, fans trust what they see and every downstream experience just works. When it isn't, the cracks show up everywhere.

Your mission is to make SeatGeek's understanding of the live event world the most accurate, comprehensive, and richly detailed in the industry — from getting brand-new onsales live the moment they're announced, to modeling complex venues seat-by-seat, to capturing the features and attributes that help fans find exactly the right spot.
SeatGeek is where passionate fans and ambitious builders come together to reshape live entertainment, and if you're excited to build the data foundation that powers it all, we'd love to hear from you.

Toptal is a global network of top talent in business, design, and technology that enables companies to scale their teams, on-demand. With $200+ million in annual revenue and team members based around the globe , Toptal is the world’s largest fully remote workforce .
We take the best elements of virtual teams and combine them with a support structure that encourages innovation, social interaction, and fun. We see no borders, move at a fast pace, and are never afraid to break the mold.

Our Product team builds and scales Toptal’s platform and products, working closely with our Operations and Engineering teams to support the organization’s growth. We embrace a data-focused approach to ensure each initiative on our product roadmap delivers a meaningful impact on our business and users. Our innovative technology platform enables us to deliver on-demand talent, without losing a human touch.
Are you a customer-centric Senior Product Manager with a proven track record of taking ownership and delivering results in a fast-paced, dynamic environment? We’re looking for a self-starting Senior Product Manager to drive innovation at Toptal by building and scaling AI-driven products that expand the breadth and depth of our product and service offering.

About Chili Piper
Chili Piper is a B2B SaaS company that helps GTM teams turn inbound leads into qualified meetings - instantly. Our Demand Conversion Platform makes it easier for buyers and sellers to connect fast, without the usual friction in the funnel.
We’re a fully remote, global team that loves building solutions that truly help our customers, moving fast, and having fun while creating something meaningful. We’re growing quickly and aiming big!
We're looking for a Senior Product Manager to lead Orchestrator, Chili Piper's GTM Control Layer.
Internally, we think of this role as a Product Market Fitter. This is not a traditional roadmap management role. It is a product leadership role for someone who loves building complex, enterprise-grade products and has the judgment to turn customer and market evidence into focused product bets that drive real adoption and business impact.
Orchestrator listens for signals across Chili Piper and external tools, decides what should happen next, and takes the action itself. That includes catching a form abandonment, a no-show, a missed meeting, or a cold chat, checking ICP fit, account ownership, intent history, and CRM state, then firing the right next step: enrolling a sequence in Salesloft, Outreach, or Gong Engage, notifying a rep, rescheduling a meeting, or sending a booking link.
You will own the full arc of a product bet: target customer, first audience, market and customer evidence, problem definition, intended outcome, value, viability, priority, success metrics, first adoption trigger, usage learning, and business outcome.
You will own the solution concept, meaning what we offer and how it is offered. You will not own solution architecture, implementation, or product enablement execution. You will partner closely with a Product Designer and a Product Engineering Lead to shape solutions that are valuable, coherent, and practical to deliver.
This role requires strong judgment, comfort with ambiguity, and the ability to turn complex workflows, data, and customer needs into clear product direction. It is a strong fit for someone who wants to build products that solve real problems for sophisticated users and who measures success by whether customers actually adopt what gets built.

Own Orchestrator end to end, from market and customer evidence through adoption, iteration, and long-term business impact
Define the first audience for every bet and protect that focus as new requests, edge cases, and opportunities emerge
Identify the right problems to solve and turn signal detection, decisioning, and action-taking into clear product direction
Define value, viability, priority, and success metrics, including what should trigger first adoption
Monitor adoption and real usage after launch, then use what you learn to improve the product and shape what comes next
Keep signal types, decision logic, and external integrations coherent, so the system stays predictable and trustworthy as it grows
Partner with Product Design on the experience, first-use path, and product-side enablement
Partner with the Product Engineering Lead on solutions that are technically sound and practical to deliver
Prioritize ruthlessly and make clear calls when the problem is complex and the answer is not obvious
Hold a high standard for quality. You do not ship things you would not want to use yourself

Senior-level experience managing complex B2B SaaS products, with clear ownership of a product area or major initiatives
Strong product judgment, with the ability to find problems worth solving and make informed tradeoffs in ambiguous environments
Hands-on use of AI tools in day-to-day product work, with good judgment about where AI genuinely improves a product experience
The ability to simplify complexity and turn customer evidence, data, and technical constraints into clear product decisions
Deep curiosity about users and markets, and a habit of building conviction through direct evidence
Comfort in technical domains and credibility with technical users and engineering partners
A bias toward focus and shipping narrow to learn quickly
Experience working closely with Engineering, Design, and cross-functional partners in a fast-moving environment
The drive to build products that solve real problems and get used, not just shipped

Experience building or owning third-party integrations, especially with CRM, Sales Engagement, or conferencing platforms
Experience with lead routing, distribution, or assignment logic
Experience with CRM or marketing automation platforms
Experience building enterprise-grade, data-rich SaaS products
Experience building or shipping with Claude or similar products
Who this role is for
This role is best suited to someone energized by high ownership, independent judgment, and making decisions without a playbook. We give people real responsibility and a lot of room to operate, which means you will be expected to run your area, set direction, and make hard calls with imperfect information.
If you are looking for a highly directed environment with a lot of structure around what to do next, this is probably not the right fit.
How this role works
We care deeply about clear ownership and close cross-functional partnership.
The Product Market Fitter owns the target customer, problem, intended outcome, value, viability, priority, adoption, and business result
The Product Designer owns the experience and product-side enablement
The Product Designer and Product Engineering Lead jointly own solution architecture
The Product Engineering Lead owns the technical solution and delivery execution

Über die Position
Gestalte mit uns die digitale Infrastruktur des europäischen Gartenbaus
Connected Growers entwickelt June: Die Plattform, über die Erzeuger, Käufer und Vermarkter effizient zusammenarbeiten. Wir ersetzen fragmentierte Prozesse durch moderne Software und schaffen eine gemeinsame digitale Infrastruktur für eine ganze Branche.
Dafür suchen wir einen Product Manager (m/w/d) für unseren Bereich Grower Experience, der gemeinsam mit Engineering und Design unsere Anwendung für Gartenbaubetriebe weiterentwickelt.
Deine Rolle bei June
Als Product Manager Grower Experience (m/w/d) verantwortest du die Produktentwicklung unserer Anwendung für Gärtner*innen. Du berichtest direkt an unseren CPO.
Deine Nutzer sind Gartenbaubetriebe, deren Bedürfnisse Du durch enge Zusammenarbeit mit diesen und weiteren Experten der Branche kennenlernst. Du entwickelst daraus technische Lösungen und Standards für die Branche.
Du definierst relevante KPIs für deinen Produktbereich und misst den Erfolg deiner Arbeit konsequent an ihnen.
Anforderungen
Was du mitbringst
Mindestens 4–5 Jahre Erfahrung im Produktmanagement von B2B-Softwareprodukten.
Erfahrung im eigenständigen Führen von User Interviews, Bereitschaft zu unregelmäßigen Vor-Ort-Besuchen bei Gärtner*innen. (Führerschein erforderlich)
Kenntnisse gängiger Tracking- und Analytics-Tools.
Exzellente schriftliche Kommunikation (Roadmaps, PRDs).
AI-Erfahrung am Puls der Zeit: Du bist bei neuen Entwicklungen up-to-date und findest wege, wie du AI für Deine Arbeit und eingebettet im Softwareteam effizient nutzen kannst.
Fließend Deutsch, sehr gutes Englisch.
Das wäre ein Plus
Erfahrung mit Prozessen aus der Warenwirtschaft oder aus dem Handel.
Ein Software-Background kombiniert mit Product-Management-Erfahrung.
Aufgabenbereich
Was du bei uns bewegst
Du verantwortest die Produktstrategie und -roadmap für den Bereich Grower Experience.
Du sprichst wöchentlich eigenständig mit unseren Gärtner*innen, baust Beziehungen zu ihnen auf und triffst die Betriebe in unregelmäßigen Abständen auch vor Ort.
Du arbeitest eng mit Design und Engineering zusammen, leitest gemeinsam mit Design User Interviews und übersetzt die daraus gewonnenen Erkenntnisse in konkrete Produktentscheidungen, während Du das Team fachlich durch den gesamten Produktentwicklungsprozess führst.
Du verstehst und artikulierst den Business Value deiner Produktentscheidungen, u. a. über KPI-Frameworks, und nutzt Tracking- und Analytics-Daten, um Annahmen zu validieren und Produktentscheidungen datenbasiert zu treffen.
Du kommunizierst Roadmaps, PRDs und Produktentscheidungen klar und überzeugend – schriftlich wie mündlich.
Du nutzt AI selbstverständlich in deinem Alltag – für Prototyping, eigene Datenanalysen und einen effizienten, AI-gestützten Produktentwicklungsprozess gemeinsam mit deinem Engineering-Team.
Deine Arbeit hat direkten Einfluss auf unser Produkt, unsere Kunden und den Erfolg von June.
So arbeiten wir
Unsere Produktteams verantworten ihre Bereiche vollständig: von der Produktstrategie über User Research und Priorisierung bis hin zum Release und den kommerziellen KPIs ihres Bereichs.
Gemeinsam mit Design und Engineering übernehmt ihr Verantwortung für den Erfolg eures Produktbereichs und arbeitet kontinuierlich daran, ihn zu verbessern.
Wir sprechen regelmäßig mit unseren Kunden, besuchen sie vor Ort und testen unsere Lösungen gemeinsam mit ihnen. Wir glauben, dass gute Produktentscheidungen nur entstehen, wenn man die Probleme der Nutzer wirklich versteht.
Wir arbeiten pragmatisch, treffen Entscheidungen früh und passen sie an, wenn neue Erkenntnisse entstehen. Wir haben starke Meinungen, halten aber nicht dogmatisch an ihnen fest. Verantwortung endet bei uns nicht mit dem Release.

Was dich erwartet
Die Möglichkeit, Produktverantwortung für einen der zentralen Bereiche von June zu übernehmen.
Die Chance, den europäischen Gartenbau grundlegend zu verändern
Ein erfahrenes Design, Product und Engineering-Team an deiner Seite.
Großer Gestaltungsspielraum für Produktstrategie und Roadmap.
Viel Verantwortung und kurze Entscheidungswege.
Modernes, AI-gestütztes Arbeiten im gesamten Produktentwicklungsprozess.
Die Möglichkeit, unsere Produktkultur aktiv mitzugestalten.
Hybrides Arbeiten in unserem Büro in Köln sowie regelmäßige Besuche bei den Gärtner*innen vor Ort.

About Lucidya
Lucidya is an AI-native platform for customer experience (CX) intelligence that helps organizations understand, engage, and retain customers at scale.
Unlike traditional platforms that stop at reporting and dashboards, Lucidya combines proprietary AI, deep language understanding, and autonomous workflows to help organizations move from insight to action. Our technology is built in-house and trained on millions of multilingual customer conversations, enabling brands across the MENA region to make better decisions, deliver better experiences, and build stronger customer relationships.
As AI reshapes how businesses operate, we're building products that make customer understanding faster, more accurate, and more actionable than ever before.
Why This Role Matters
Most organizations today are overwhelmed with customer data.
Conversations are happening across social media, surveys, reviews, support tickets, messaging channels, and countless other touchpoints. The challenge isn't collecting the data anymore. It's knowing what matters and what to do next.
The Monitoring & Research domain sits at the center of that challenge.
This is where customers come to understand public perception, identify emerging trends, monitor competitors, measure customer sentiment, and uncover the insights that drive business decisions. It is one of the most strategically important parts of Lucidya 's platform and one of the biggest opportunities for innovation as AI transforms how research and customer intelligence are done.
As Senior Product Manager, you'll be responsible for shaping how thousands of users discover, trust, and act on insights generated from millions of customer conversations.
You'll be joining a team that values ownership over hierarchy, customer outcomes over feature output, and learning over certainty. We move quickly, challenge assumptions, and expect product leaders to bring strong opinions while remaining open to changing their minds when the evidence says otherwise.
If you're excited by complex customer problems, AI-powered products, and the opportunity to define the future of customer intelligence in a region where world-class solutions are still emerging, this role will give you significant room to make an impact.

Own the future of Monitoring & Research at Lucidya
You'll define the vision, strategy, and roadmap across three key product areas:
Social Listening
Managed Channels Analytics
Voice of Customer (VoC)
Your responsibility isn't simply delivering features. It's ensuring customers can confidently answer critical business questions about their customers, markets, competitors, and brand performance.
Turn customer signals into decisions
You'll spend significant time understanding how customers currently make decisions, where they struggle to find trustworthy insights, and what prevents them from taking action.
You'll use those learnings to build products that help customers move beyond reporting and toward clear recommendations, meaningful insights, and measurable business outcomes.
Lead discovery before delivery
You'll challenge assumptions, validate problems, and ensure we're solving issues that matter before resources are committed.
You'll regularly engage customers, prospects, Customer Success teams, and internal stakeholders to uncover opportunities and validate product direction.
Success in this role means building the right thing, not simply building things quickly.
Raise the quality bar for AI-powered insights
As AI becomes increasingly central to our platform, you'll help define what "trustworthy AI" means in practice.
You'll work closely with AI, Data, Design, and Engineering teams to improve:
Insight accuracy
Sentiment quality
Explainability
Relevance
Customer trust
You'll constantly ask whether an insight is genuinely useful, not just technically impressive.
Make difficult prioritization decisions
Not every good idea belongs on the roadmap.
You'll evaluate opportunities using customer feedback, product data, market insights, commercial priorities, and strategic impact.
You'll make trade-offs transparently and help the organization understand why certain bets are worth making while others are not.
Drive product adoption and business impact
You'll closely monitor customer behavior, adoption patterns, retention drivers, churn signals, and feedback loops.
You'll use those insights to continuously improve the product and ensure the work being delivered creates measurable value for both customers and the business.
Be a leader beyond product
You'll collaborate across Engineering, Design, AI, Customer Success, Sales, Marketing, and Leadership teams.
You'll help create alignment, provide clarity during ambiguity, and contribute to building a culture where teams are empowered to solve problems rather than simply execute requirements.

You have strong product fundamentals
You have at least 5 years of product management experience, ideally within B2B SaaS environments.
You know how to take a problem from discovery through validation, delivery, measurement, and iteration.
You understand that product management is ultimately about creating customer and business value, not managing backlogs.
You simplify complexity
You're comfortable working with large datasets, analytics platforms, AI-powered products, or technically complex systems.
More importantly, you know how to transform complexity into experiences that feel intuitive and useful to customers.
You stay close to customers
You don't rely solely on internal opinions to make decisions.
You regularly speak with customers, investigate workflows, validate assumptions, and seek evidence before committing to a direction.
You're naturally curious about how people work and where products create friction in their lives.

Anyone can build AI insurance software now. The models are commoditized. The demos work. Almost nobody starts where Agency Revolution starts: thousands of independent P&C agencies already paying us to communicate with their clients, plus deep integrations into the systems where agency data actually lives.
The opportunity is the relationship layer — the system that notices when an agency's clients are at risk of churning, spots the cross-sell opportunity, picks the right message and channel and moment, and acts. We call it RelationshipOS. For ten years, agencies have trusted us to speak to their clients.

Now we're expanding what we can see: call transcripts, carrier communications, life events. The policies live in the agency's management system. The relationship lives with us. Nobody else has both the permission and the infrastructure.
We know what we're betting on. We don't yet know what makes an agency owner act on it. That's the job.
The strategic thesis is set. What's unresolved is whether it's true — whether an agency will actually change what they do because our system told them to, and what has to be built for that to happen. You're hired to answer that by shipping, not by studying.

s.h: Two halves, and you need both
s.t:
You personally build the bet. The intelligence layer is your work. Discovery with agency owners, prototypes in front of them within days, the smallest version that proves someone will act. Much of this is assembled rather than authored — the right vendor wired into AR Connect and pointed at a real use case will beat anything we could build from scratch this year. You don't hand this half to your team; it's too early and too ambiguous to delegate.
Your team drives the day-to-day execution and health of the existing platform. Two Product Owners and a Product Analyst keep a profitable, decade-old product healthy and improving. You set their priorities, strengthen their product judgment, raise their craft, and shield them from thrash. You remain the primary product manager responsible for the roadmap, discovery, and strategic product decisions. Done well, this is what buys you the time to do the first half.
Most people are good at one of these. We need someone who won't quietly abandon the other.
This position offers $125,000-$140,000 depending on experience and qualifications.

RelationshipOS — the intelligence layer. Churn signals. Cross-sell opportunities. Adaptive customer journeys instead of rigid sequences. You define what "acted on" means, instrument it, and are accountable for the number.
AR Connect and the vendor stack. AR Connect is our integration layer — where APIs pull in calls, carrier communications, life events, and other signals, and where third-party capability plugs into our distribution. It's the substrate the whole thesis sits on, and it's how a promising vendor becomes a live use case in front of agencies.
That work is yours: mapping the landscape of management systems, carrier connections, data enrichment providers, and AI vendors; deciding what we integrate versus build; running the POCs; and getting from "interesting demo" to something an agency actually uses. Data quality, latency, unit economics, and what happens when a vendor's model is wrong are your problems to surface early. You shape the deals and bring the recommendation — the SVP and our partnership team close them.
Voice AI as a channel. Not a feature — a real channel. Define the MVP, run pilots where AI handles outbound outreach with warm handoffs to agencies, and produce the evidence for whether this moves us from subscription toward outcome-based pricing.
The Agency Revolution roadmap. What ships, in what order, and what we stop doing. You own the sequencing and defend it.

Constructor powers product search and discovery for some of the largest retailers in the world. We serve billions of requests every week, and you’ve probably seen our results somewhere and used our product without knowing it.

We differentiate ourselves by focusing on metrics over features, and reinventing search and discovery from the ground up as a machine learning challenge with the specific goal of improving metrics like revenue. We’re approximately doubling year over year despite the market slowing down and have customers in every eCommerce vertical.

We’re a passionate team of technologists who love solving problems and want to make our customers’ and coworkers’ lives better. We value empathy, openness, curiosity, continuous improvement, and are excited by metrics that matter. We believe that empowering everyone in a company to do what they think is best can lead to great things.

We’re looking for a highly technical, systems-minded Senior Product Manager to lead two critical search intelligence teams: Machine Learning & Recall and Query . Search at Constructor is fundamentally an ML challenge, and this role sits at the absolute entry point of our discovery pipeline, right where shopper intent meets candidate retrieval.
In this role, you will bridge the Query team (understanding what a shopper means across intent, entities, and language) with the Machine Learning & Recall team (retrieving the exact right set of candidate products across massive catalogs).

You will define strategy across both domains, balancing state-of-the-art techniques, such as vector search, semantic parsing, dense embeddings, and LLM-assisted query interpretation, with low-latency production execution.

You won’t be measured on shipping features for the sake of it; you’ll be measured on candidate quality, query accuracy, and driving business outcomes like conversion rate, search-attributed revenue, and revenue per visit.

Set a unified roadmap: Define the multi-quarter vision and strategy across both the Machine Learning & Recall and Query teams, ensuring query understanding and candidate generation evolve hand-in-hand.
Drive Query intelligence: Lead the Query team to push boundaries in tokenization, spell correction, entity extraction, intent classification, and LLM-assisted query parsing across multiple languages.
Advance Recall systems: Lead the Machine Learning & Recall team in evolving candidate generation architecture, seamlessly combining traditional keyword search with modern dense embeddings, vector retrieval, and hybrid recall models.
Move core business metrics: Own measurable lift in search-attributed conversion, revenue per visit, and GMV across all retail customer verticals.
Turn research into production wins: Work shoulder-to-shoulder with ML researchers, data scientists, and software engineers to take SOTA models from research to low-latency, cost-effective production systems.
Balance ML performance trade-offs: Make data-backed decisions balancing model complexity, accuracy, inference latency, compute costs, and real-time execution constraints.
Build evaluation frameworks: Establish robust offline and online measurement systems to evaluate retrieval precision and query understanding accuracy against customer revenue outcomes.
Orchestrate pipeline handoffs: Ensure candidate product sets and query context flow cleanly into downstream ranking and search quality models without signal loss.
Solve systemic issues: Lead technical triage when query interpretation or retrieval anomalies occur, building durable, automated fixes rather than one-off patches.
What Success Looks Like

s.h: Within your first year, you will have
s.t:
Evolved our hybrid recall framework to measurably improve candidate generation precision for long-tail queries and complex catalog structures.
Driven quantifiable lift in search-attributed conversion and revenue per visit across major customer verticals.
Stood up an integrated evaluation framework connecting query parsing and candidate recall directly to business outcomes.
Optimized inference latency and compute infrastructure to ensure high-capacity ML models run fast and cost-effectively in production.

This role starts on the content platform, and the platform surface it serves is growing. The foundations of the company, identity and access, developer platform, data and the infrastructure everything runs on, are being invested in over the coming year. We are looking for someone whose curiosity does not stop at the edge of their own team, because the interesting problems here sit exactly where those layers meet.
There is genuine ambiguity in this space right now, and a decision or two you would inherit that we have not finished making. We would rather tell you that than have you discover it in month two. The upside is that very little here is set, so the person who takes this shapes the layer everything else in the product is built on for the next several years.

Own the content services every surface depends on. The services and APIs that serve content to the learner surface, the admin surface and everything we build next, plus the delivery path including CDN and video, and file and asset storage.
Own the structural contract. How content is stored, versioned and served so it can be reused and assembled differently for different customers. This is a schema and interface problem before it is a tooling problem, and your measure is whether the contract other teams build against is clear, stable and safe to change.
Own multi tenant separation. Making sure one customer’s content and branding stay theirs. The tenancy model needs a decision and an owner, and that will be one of your first real pieces of work.
Own access, entitlements and data residency. Who can reach what, where data lives, and what we are able to commit to contractually.
Own performance and cost per tenant. If this layer is slow, everything is slow. If it is expensive, it is expensive everywhere.
Carry the platform half of a migration already in flight. We are moving off an incumbent content tool while the current system keeps earning. Sequencing that is the real work, and the order matters more than the ambition.
Own the non functional questions that show up in deals. A meaningful share of our deals slow down in security and compliance review rather than in the pitch, and that is a product problem with a revenue number attached.

s.h: This role is for you if you have
s.t:
Experience with content management as a product, whether that is a CMS, a DAM, a headless content platform or a structured content system at scale. This is our primary preference.
Experience owning platform or infrastructure adjacent product, where success was measured in what other teams could build rather than in features a customer names.
Enough technical depth to be useful and the honesty to say where you are not. You can read an architecture proposal, ask the question that unpicks it, and tell the difference between a researched answer and a fluent one.
The ability to hold your own with senior engineers, infrastructure engineers and security specialists. Not as a peer on implementation, but well enough that a remediation estimate or a tenancy design does not go unchallenged. A previous career as an engineer is a real advantage and not a requirement.
A habit of thinking in seams. Where systems meet, what a contract between them should guarantee, and how to keep a decision reversible rather than walking through a one way door.
The ability to sequence. We are modernising a platform that carries real history while it keeps earning, and the order matters more than the ambition.
Writing. Decisions, tradeoffs and the reasoning behind them, in a way an engineer and an executive can both act on.
Nice to have, and genuinely useful: depth in AI and personalisation, or in infrastructure. Either one compounds with this role, and we are not expecting both.

s.h: This role is not for you if
s.t:
You want to be a delivery manager for the engineers. They are strong and they do not need coordinating. They need decisions and clarity about what matters.
You want to own the authoring and editorial experience itself. A colleague owns that, you will work closely with them, and drawing the seam between you well is part of the job.
You want to run a rewrite programme. Foundations serve outcomes, and a foundation with no customer outcome attached does not get funded here and should not.
You need the surrounding decisions settled before you arrive.

About Oula
Oula Health is a venture-backed, midwifery-led maternity and GYN care company building the next generation of women's healthcare. We partner exclusively with major health systems — including Mount Sinai, Stamford Health, and Novant Health — to embed our collaborative OB-GYN and midwifery model directly inside their networks. We're a team of ~100 people at Series B stage, with 4 clinics today and three more opening in 2026.

At Oula, our product doesn't sit alongside our EHR — it integrates directly into it. Every product and engineering decision has downstream consequences for how our EHRs are configured, and every EHR configuration decision shapes what's possible on the product side. Someone has to hold both at once.
We're looking for a technically-minded Product Manager to own and evolve our core technology stack — including our EHR, patient portal, and care management platform. This role sits at the intersection of product, operations, and health system integration, serving as the internal and external subject matter expert on our EMR and the primary lead for health system EHR integrations.
You'll manage the day-to-day health of our tech stack, partnering closely with both internal teams and external health system stakeholders to ensure our systems run smoothly and our integrations deliver.

You can sit with a midwife and understand why a clinical template matters, then turn around and write a bug ticket that engineering can actually action, then build the SOP so the next market launch doesn't require you to be in the room. When things are ambiguous (and they often are), you'll lean in rather than wait for clarity.
What You'll Own
EHR Configuration & Clinical Systems
Own day-to-day management of our core tech stack: the EHR, patient portal, and care management platform
Own Athena and Epic configuration end to end: clinical templates, order sets, lab configurations, payer connectivity, and access management for clinical and ops staff
Lead EHR integration efforts as the internal and external subject matter expert — FHIR/HL7 data exchange, health system IT coordination and committed go-live timelines
Own and accelerate Epic integration timelines as we onboard additional health system partners
Maintain configuration integrity as new markets launch and care model workflows evolve
Partner with our IT team on infrastructure; own the clinical systems layer they don't touch
Product Operations & Launch
Own bug intake and prioritization from Market Operations — standardize how Engineering receives, scopes, and resolves issues and communicates status back to the field
Build structured launch toolkits and training materials so clinic teams are prepared for new feature rollouts on day one
Coordinate end-to-end launches across Product, Engineering, and Operations
Identify where AI and automation can reduce manual administrative burden in product operations workflows
Standards & Knowledge Management
Build and maintain the clinical systems SOP library so new market setup is repeatable — documented well enough that a new hire can execute without you in the room
Develop onboarding materials for clinic managers and clinical staff on EHR workflows and tooling
Drive feature parity efforts so patients and clinicians experience a consistent standard of care across markets
Data & Reporting
Build and maintain dashboards tracking feature adoption, issue resolution, and rollout health across clinics
Develop quarterly reporting for Product, leadership, and health system partners on platform performance
Ensure data infrastructure is in place to measure the impact of every feature rollout

3+ years with product operations, technical program management, or PM-adjacent work — ideally at a growth-stage digital health or services company
Strong problem-solving instincts and genuine curiosity — you like figuring out how things work and making them work better
Ease with ambiguity and a bias toward action; this role requires you to create the playbook, not execute someone else's
Demonstrated ability to navigate complex stakeholder environments and drive aggressive timelines — ideally with client-facing or health system-facing experience
Ability to speak ‘multiple languages’ – comfort going deep on technical details while communicating clearly to non-technical audiences; you can write a bug ticket, an SOP, and a launch plan that people actually follow; hands-on EHR configuration and integration experience strongly preferred
Analytical enough to build a dashboard and identify a pattern, even if you're not a SQL expert
What Success Looks Like
In your first 90 days, you've audited our current Athena configuration, identified gaps, and have a remediation plan. You understand the bug triage process well enough to have improved it. You've met your counterparts at every health system partner and know what's coming for the next Epic integration.
At six months, new market launches have a repeatable systems and product checklist. Clinic teams know what to expect before a feature goes live. Bug resolution time is measurably faster and the field is no longer sending issues into a black hole.
At one year, the SOP library is comprehensive, clinical systems configuration is stable and documented, and you've successfully navigated at least one new health system EHR environment. The product team has a reliable partner and the ops team isn't dependent on any single person for systems knowledge.
